summary: Target state of the community server as data. Nothing here is applied to a server; applying it is a later unit with the operator.

metrics.measures: How many members hold one role.
metrics.source: The platform's count of members per role. No message is read and no member id is kept.

metrics.measures: How many days have passed since the last message in one channel.
metrics.source: The time carried by the id of the channel's last message. No message is read and no member id is kept.

roles.name: @everyone
roles.purpose: Every member. The base of all permissions.

roles.name: Operator
roles.purpose: Runs the server and is the last instance for every decision.

roles.name: Moderator
roles.purpose: Removes content and times members out. Decides unclear cases before the operator.

roles.name: Diallak
roles.purpose: The role of the bot's application.

roles.name: Subject guide: coding
roles.purpose: The visible helper for coding questions. Carries no moderation right.

roles.name: Subject guide: video
roles.purpose: The visible helper for video questions. Carries no moderation right.

roles.name: Contributor
roles.purpose: First step of the contributor ladder: a contribution of this member was merged. Credited in releases.

roles.name: Supporter
roles.purpose: A thank-you for financial support. Nothing attaches to it.

roles.name: Supporter for 3 months
roles.purpose: A thank-you for support over time. Nothing attaches to it. The step of three months is a proposal.

roles.name: Supporter for 6 months
roles.purpose: A thank-you for support over time. Nothing attaches to it. The step of six months is a proposal.

roles.name: Supporter for a year
roles.purpose: A thank-you for support over time. Nothing attaches to it. The step of twelve months is a proposal.

categories.name: Community
categories.purpose: Talk, help and the private path to the operator.

categories.name: Areas
categories.purpose: Topic rooms that open at a threshold and close when they stay empty.

categories.name: Languages
categories.purpose: One social room per language, opened at a threshold.

channels.name: rules
channels.purpose: The server rules with links to the code of conduct, the privacy notice and the imprint. Read-only.

channels.name: announcements
channels.purpose: Own releases and security advisories, as they happen. Read-only.

channels.name: lounge
channels.purpose: One relaxed room for everything around the projects.

channels.name: support
channels.purpose: Questions, one post each. The bot answers a new post first with excerpts from the documentation; people answer after it.

channels.name: tickets
channels.purpose: The private path next to e-mail: a member opens a private thread addressed to the operator. Nobody writes in the channel itself.

channels.name: espanol
channels.purpose: Social room in Spanish. Technical channels and support stay in English.

channels.name: deutsch

channels.name: italiano

channels.name: Events
channels.purpose: Voice for scheduled events: office hours, demo days, game nights. Closed between events; push-to-talk.

channels.name: mod-queue
channels.purpose: Cases the platform's filter flagged, for the moderators.

channels.name: mod-log
channels.purpose: The trail of moderator actions, for the operator to read.

opening.subject: interest-home-lab
opening.reasoning: A room needs enough people that a message gets an answer the same day. Twelve interested members, on every daily reading for two weeks, is a first guess; it is replaced once the lounge shows how many interested members a daily conversation takes.

closing.subject: home-lab
closing.reasoning: A room whose last message is a month old makes the server look deserted. Thirty days is a first guess.

opening.subject: interest-media
opening.reasoning: Same reasoning as for the home lab area; the value is a first guess and is not measured.

areas.name: Spanish social room
conditions: A moderator or subject guide who reads Spanish has agreed to watch the room.

opening.subject: lang-es
opening.reasoning: A language room is social, so fewer people carry it than a topic room. Five members who asked for it, on every daily reading for two weeks, is a first guess. The room also needs a person who can read it, because nobody can moderate a language they do not read.

closing.subject: room-es

automation.what: Answers the ask command from the documentation, visible only to the member who asked.
Reads the first message of a new post in the support forum and replies first with excerpts, unless the post carries the opt-out tag.
Shows new discussions of the listed repositories on the server with a link back.
Puts flagged cases in front of the moderators and writes the trail of their actions.
Opens and closes the threshold areas and language rooms from the readings of their rules. Until it is built, the operator does this by hand.
Posts own releases and security advisories as they happen, and everything else as one digest per channel per day.
Gives and takes the supporter roles from the funding platforms.
Filters spam and obvious abuse before a person sees it.
Asks a new member the onboarding questions and gives the roles of the chosen options.
Invites people and grants the moderator, subject guide and contributor roles. The bot grants none of them.
Reads and answers the private threads in the ticket channel.
Schedules events and opens the voice room for their duration.
Applies this definition to the server. A later unit with the operator.
